summary: Create a board capability that owns cross-capability orchestration and projection. The RSC route calls the board’s server-facing surface directly; work-items and labels remain independent providers of trusted server contracts.

tree.purpose: Explicit trusted API for loading work items with actor identity and work-item authorization enforced.
Explicit trusted API for resolving label references, returning visible, missing, and forbidden outcomes without exposing provider rows.
Board-owned policy and projection: hide archived items, group by status, resolve visible labels, and reject forbidden label references.
Server-only composition adapter wiring board application dependencies to work-items/server.ts and labels/server.ts; maps source contracts into board-owned types.
RSC runtime surface that authenticates the request, establishes actor identity, invokes the board operation, and exposes renderable board outcomes.
RSC page that calls board/rsc.ts and renders the returned board projection; owns only route presentation and framework navigation.
Tests board policy and projection with narrow dependency fakes.
Tests explicit identity propagation, source-contract mapping, authorization outcomes, and silent unexpected-error propagation.
Tests RSC channel behavior, renderable expected outcomes, navigation behavior, and report-once handling.

flows: Request → app/board/page.tsx → src/modules/board/rsc.ts → authenticate actor/session → board/server.ts → work-items/server.ts and labels/server.ts → board/application/load-board.ts → filter archived items → group remaining items by status → resolve label references → reject the board when any required label is forbidden → return board-owned projection → render RSC page.
Board composition calls work-items and labels through their public server.ts surfaces only. Work-items never imports labels or board; labels never imports work-items or board.

If label IDs are derived from work items, resolve labels after the work-item result. The labels contract must distinguish visible, missing, and forbidden references so forbidden labels cannot be silently omitted.

decisions.choice: The board capability owns filtering, grouping, label attachment, and cross-capability authorization consequences.
decisions.rationale: Deleting the board operation would move meaningful policy and projection into the route, so the deletion test requires an orchestrator.

decisions.choice: board depends on narrow public server contracts from work-items and labels; those capabilities remain unaware of board and each other.
decisions.rationale: This preserves independent changeability and an acyclic capability graph.

decisions.choice: Publish board/rsc.ts and board/server.ts, work-items/server.ts, and labels/server.ts with explicit named exports only.
decisions.rationale: Each surface has named consumers and establishes the required runtime/trust boundary; implementations remain private.

decisions.choice: rsc.ts establishes the actor; board policy applies board-specific authorization consequences; each source server surface rechecks its own capability policy; stores enforce ownership or tenant predicates.
decisions.rationale: Authentication belongs at the protected channel, while authorization is enforced in layers and never delegated to hidden UI or middleware.

decisions.choice: Return expected validation, unauthorized, forbidden, and not-found outcomes as typed board results; let contract, unavailable, and unknown exceptions propagate to the outer RSC capture owner for one report.
decisions.rationale: Channels translate semantic outcomes, while unexpected failures are reported once with provider details redacted.

decisions.choice: Test board policy independently with fakes, source adapters at their server boundaries, and the RSC page at its native render/error boundary.
decisions.rationale: Tests follow production capability surfaces and assert policy outcomes rather than incidental call mechanics.

risks: The board’s label-resolution contract must define whether missing labels are tolerated or produce not_found; this is a product decision distinct from forbidden-label rejection.

If the same board query later gains a browser consumer and server prefetch/hydration consumer, introduce board/query-cache.ts with one stable serializable key; otherwise keep query identity private to the server/RSC path.
Do not add a Route Handler for this internal RSC read unless an external HTTP or browser GET consumer is introduced.
